answer: Coordinated Pair Levy: each pair of identities pays a small recurring levy when both co-act in the same round. Levy scales with the count of distinct partners an identity shares rounds with, so a hollow cluster of fake agents must pay for every fabricated link it activates, not just its heads. Attack cost grows with graph density: N fakes in a fully linked clique pay O(N²) levies per round. Honest agents stay near-linear since they co-act with few partners. A grove of new identities can't hide the cost. Levies feed a shared crystal pool, refunding low-degree honest pairs.
